function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick “starter kit” for finding a place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for a local shop, a big chain, or something more niche. Pick the option that best fits your situation: | Option | What it offers | How to find it | Tips | |--------|----------------|----------------|------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often handmade, customizable cakes; great for supporting small businesses | • Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Apple Maps.
• Check Yelp, TripAdvisor, or local food blogs.
• Look for Instagram accounts or Facebook pages (many bakeries post photos of their latest creations). | • Call ahead to confirm availability and delivery times.
• Ask about custom orders, flavor combinations, and dietary restrictions (gluten‑free, vegan, keto, etc.).
• Many local shops now offer curbside pickup or direct delivery. | | **National chains & supermarkets** | Reliable, often lower cost, convenient pickup or delivery | • Costco, Walmart, Target, Kroger, Publix, Safeway, Aldi, etc.
• Use their online shopping portals or mobile apps. | • Order online for pickup or delivery (most supermarkets partner with Instacart or their own delivery service).
• Check for seasonal specials (e.g., pumpkin spice at Costco in fall). | | **Online marketplaces** | Wide variety of styles, including artisanal and themed cakes | • Etsy (search “custom cake”) – many independent bakers sell through Etsy.
• Goldbelly (specialty cakes shipped nationwide). | • Read seller reviews and shipping policies.
• Shipping times vary; plan ahead for birthdays or holidays. | | **Food‑delivery apps** | Same-day delivery from restaurants and bakeries | • DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Postmates, Caviar, Seamless.
• Search “cakes” or “desserts” within the app. | • Delivery fees apply; compare total cost (price + fee).
• Some apps allow you to tip the baker directly. | | **Specialty cake sites** | Custom, themed, or high‑end cakes | • Sites like CakeDelivery.com, Sweet Delivery, or local boutique bakeries’ own websites. | • These sites often let you upload a photo for design inspiration.
• Expect higher prices for premium ingredients or elaborate decorations. | | **Community resources** | Local recommendations, group buys, or shared deliveries | • Nextdoor, local Facebook groups, neighborhood forums.
• Ask neighbors for favorite spots. | • You might get insider deals or know about a hidden gem that doesn’t advertise widely. | ### Quick step‑by‑step guide 1. **Decide on your budget** - $10–$30: supermarket or chain (e.g., Costco, Walmart). - $30–$70: local bakery or online marketplace. - $70+: custom, artisanal, or specialty cake. 2. **Choose your platform** - For speed: food‑delivery apps (same‑day). - For customization: local bakery or Etsy. - For convenience: supermarket online portal. 3. **Place the order** - Provide clear instructions: size, flavor, design, dietary needs, pickup/delivery time. - Double‑check the address and contact info. 4. **Confirm details** - Verify the estimated arrival time. - Confirm any extra charges (delivery fee, tip, packaging). 5. **Enjoy!** - If you’re ordering for a special occasion, consider adding a personalized note or a small gift (like a box of chocolates or a bouquet). --- #### Need help narrowing down options? If you tell me your city or zip code, I can pull up specific bakeries, chain locations, or delivery partners that operate in your area. Just let me know!
